species.name: Golden toad
species.habitat: Cloud forest and temporary breeding pools.
species.threat_summary: ENSO-related drought and disease have been proposed; attribution specifically to human-caused warming is disputed.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 14–19 °C; RH >90 %: no tolerance source in the brief.

scenario.title: Which option best matches the regional climate cycle?
scenario.period_note: Educational recreation set in 2015 with the 1981–2014 archive; it does not assume the species was still alive or that these data were available at the time.
scenario.question: Compare the 12 typical months of the three variables. Choose the candidate with the smallest standardized climate distance.
scenario.model_rule: Mean of the 12-month RMSE per variable divided by the reference site’s 1981–2014 monthly standard deviation; three equal weights. A teaching rule, not an ecological model.
scenario.feedback: The lowest index identifies the regional climate analogue among these three options. p-values test for trends, not suitability. Still needed: mist, pool hydroperiod, forest cover, chytrid fungus.
scenario.limitations: The plots and management conditions are fictional. This is not a translocation recommendation or a survival prediction.
scenario.game_assumptions: To compare climate, all candidates are assumed to have otherwise equivalent and suitable conditions; this has not been checked in the field.

variables.label: Mean air temperature
variables.aggregation: Day-weighted annual mean of monthly means

variables.label: Dry-season rainfall
variables.aggregation: Rainfall summed over the location's 4 driest months (1981–2025 average cycle)

key_variables.brief_favorable_conditions: Constant mist (humidity > 90 %), cool temperatures (14–19 °C), predictable seasonal rain and clean temporary pools.
key_variables.why_these_variables: Mist/humidity, cool cloud-forest temperature and the dry-season rain that keeps breeding pools from drying out.
key_variables.absolute_value_caution: Cloud-forest species: the NASA grid cell averages 381 m, far below the cloud forest (around 1,500 m), so absolute temperatures and humidity are several degrees warmer/drier than the habitat. Use the change versus normal, not the absolute value.
key_variables.rainfall_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.

requirements.requirement: Cold, wet elfin cloud forest at 1,500–1,620 m
requirements.value: Elfin cloud forest on a cold, wet ridge (Brillante), 1,500–1,620 m. Humidity was never measured for the species.
requirements.evidence: Its whole range was a few km² of cold, wet ridge-top cloud forest; the >90 % humidity figure has no species-specific source.
requirements.proxy_note: Not comparable in absolute terms: NASA's cell averages 381 m. NASA values describe the regional grid cell, not the habitat itself.

requirements.value: 14–19 °C (from the project brief; no tolerance study)
requirements.evidence: No temperature tolerance was ever measured. Before the 1987 collapse, local temperature anomalies reached record highs.

sources.title: Pounds & Crump 1994, Conservation Biology: Amphibian declines and climate disturbance

requirements.proxy_note: Use the change versus normal: the NASA cell is far warmer than the ridge. NASA values describe the regional grid cell, not the habitat itself.

requirements.requirement: Shallow rain pools during the April–June breeding season
requirements.brief_value: Predictable seasonal rain and clean temporary pools
requirements.value: Rain-filled pools among tree roots, often no deeper than about 2.5 cm (one inch), that last through April–June.
requirements.evidence: Toads bred in very shallow rainwater pools; in 1987 the dry season was unusually warm and dry and local stream flow hit a record low.

sources.title: Pounds & Crump 1994, Conservation Biology: Amphibian declines and climate disturbance

requirements.proxy_note: Dry-season rainfall trend only; pool depth is not measured.

survival_card.use_rule: Only confirmed or corrected ranges may be used as hard rules in the game. Show partly_supported and no_published_data values as approximate guidance with their label.
